To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pro-(carboxespeptidases A), the binary complexes pro-(carboxpeptidase A)-pro-(proteinase E), and the monomeric caroxypeptidase species A1 and A 2 can now be prepared from pig pancreas in high yield and with high purity.

the two forms of the pig pancreatic proenzyme, pro-(carboxy-peptidase A), can be prepared more quickly than by previous methods and, after trypsin activation, the two forms of carboxypeptidine A can be obtained in high yield and in a highly purified state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the pancreatic proenzymes and of the mechanisms involved in their activation, as well as the isolation of their monomeric active enzymes.
the isolation of the two pro-(carboxy-peptidases A), their activation to the two monomeric forms of carboxypeptidease A and the study of the properties of these enzymes.
the purification and characterization of the two forms (A and B) of pro-(carboypeptidase B) from pig pancrea.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two forms of porcine pro-(carboxy peptidase A), the monomer and binary complex, are isolated from the same preparation of pancreatic tissue and that the two pro-(carboxyl peptidases A), the monomeric pro-(carboxypetidase A1) and pro-(carboxyeptidase A2), are obtained from the same preparation by controlled trypsic activation of the pro-(enzyme) forms.

the two forms of porcine pro-(carboxy-peptidase A), the binary complex with the zymogen pro-(proteinase) E and the monomers, are obtained by the method described in the present paper in a pure state and in high yield, and that the carboxypeptides A1 and A-2 species are obtained from them in monomeric and highly active form.

the two forms of the proenzyme, pro-(carboxy-peptidase A), are present in the pig pancreas in the ratio of about 3.5:1 and can be isolated in a highly purified state by a single-step chromatography on DE- AE-Sepharose at a pH of 5.7.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we now have available the two forms of the proenzyme (monomeric or complexed with proteinase E), the two forms of carboxypeptidine A (A1 or A2) and the two forms of proteinase E.
the pro-(carbonylpeptidases) can now be prepared in a few hours and that the two monomeric forms of carboxypeptides can be obtained in a few hours.
the method of preparation of pro-(carboypeptidase) A1 and A 2 described in this paper allows the preparation of these two proenzymes in a single step from a single pancreatic extract.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of DEAE-Sepharoses in the presence of 7 M-ureaturns out to be an excellent tool for the isolation of the two pig pancreatic pro-( carboxypeptidasest A) and for the preparation of the monomeric caroxypeptidases in a single-step process.

the two forms of pancreatic pro-(carboypeptidase) A, the monomer and binary complex, are easily separated and can be activated in a controlled manner by trypsin to yield monomeric carboypeptidases with a specific activity of 1,500 units/mg.

the two forms of pancreatic pro-(carboypeptidase) A can be prepared in high yield and in a very short time, by using a single purification step on DEAE-Sephaose, in a pH range where the proenzyme is stable, and without the need for a protease inhibitor.
